Wednesday, late.

Got the attendance notice from the department today. "Shortage of attendance: standard penalty applies." Standard penalty. As though I'd been bunking to sit in a cafe. I've missed eleven classes because Mum's treatment days keep landing on Tuesdays and Thursdays, and I haven't told a single teacher. What would I even say? That my family is a mess?

Aparna, who sits next to me, asked quietly at lunch why I look so tired and why I keep disappearing. I said I was fine and changed the subject. My last two test marks fell, and now this. They can't help because they don't know. And the more I hide, the more it costs.

Tarun

qa.q: How many classes has Tarun missed?
What is Tarun feeling about telling the teachers?
qa.a: Tarun feels ashamed and afraid of being judged, which is why the question of what to say leaves Tarun silent.

qa.q: What could Tarun do about the attendance notice, and why?
qa.a: Tarun could go to a teacher or the department with the notice and explain the treatment days, because the department can only adjust things it knows about.

qa.q: How might Aparna see Tarun's disappearing and tired looks?
qa.a: Aparna sees a classmate who is clearly struggling and cares enough to ask, though Aparna may feel shut out by the answer 'fine'.

grounding: Fearing judgement, the student tells the college nothing, misses classes without explanation, and standard penalties follow.

In the small town of Sirsa, Wasim's mother had been bedridden since the rains. Every morning he gave her tea, helped his younger brother get ready for school, and then took the 9:40 bus to the degree college, if he took it at all.
He told no one there. At the college gate, his classmate Saurabh asked once why he kept disappearing. "Just family stuff," Wasim said, and changed the subject. He was afraid the teachers would think he wasn't serious, or worse, feel sorry for him.
In December the notice board listed the students barred from exams for low attendance. His name was fourth. Beside it, his internal marks: failing in two subjects.
The head clerk, looking at his file, said, "There's no leave application here. No letter. We didn't know anything." Wasim stood in the office and didn't know how to begin explaining three months.

qa.q: Where was Wasim's name on the exam notice list?
qa.a: His name was fourth on the list of students barred for low attendance.

qa.q: What was Wasim afraid of when he kept silent at college?
qa.a: He was afraid the teachers would think he wasn't serious, or would feel sorry for him.

qa.q: What else could Wasim do now, even late?
qa.a: He could write to the principal with his mother's situation and ask what can still be done, because an honest late explanation is better than none.

qa.q: How does the situation look from the head clerk's side?
qa.a: The head clerk sees a file with no leave application or letter, so the college simply applied the normal rules without knowing anything.

grounding: Shows a student hiding a parent's illness, missing class without explanation, and the unaware department applying standard penalties.
